What it does for you

For fleet owners

Buy the battery your routes need, not the one in the brochure

Too small and a truck does not finish a winter shift. Too big and you pay for weight you never use. EV Scope sizes the battery, the chargers and the grid connection from your own routes, before you order.

What you get answered

  • How much battery do our vehicles actually need?
  • Will they finish a full winter shift?
  • Do we have to upgrade the grid connection?

Documents you can take away

See all six

Example

Six refuse trucks on a 120 km city round with 400 stops. Each needs a 370 kWh battery. The depot peaks at 166 kW, inside the 400 kW it already has.

Sample case with illustrative figures. Open this case in the demo

For housing associations

From 2026, residents have the right to charge

When everyone plugs in after work, the supply to the building sets the limit. EV Scope shows how much charging it can carry today, and what a larger connection would take.

What you get answered

  • How much charging can our supply actually carry?
  • What happens when everyone plugs in after work?
  • Do we need a larger incoming connection?

Documents you can take away

A car park on one shared supply. You see how many charge points fit today, what the evening looks like when everyone is home, and the connection size the rest would need.

For municipalities

A tender that holds, inside a budget that is already fixed

You buy in fixed budget years and cannot favour a brand. EV Scope turns your routes into requirements that every bidder is measured against, and shows which vehicles can switch now and which should wait.

What you get answered

  • Which vehicles can we electrify now, and which wait?
  • Can we spread the spend across budget years?
  • Will this hold up if a supplier complains?

For truck makers and charge operators

Show the buyer it works on their routes, not on a test cycle

Buyers ask whether your truck finishes their hardest winter day, and still does at year 8. EV Scope runs your spec on their routes, on the same case as every other bid. Charge operators get the load of the depot hour by hour, to size the site and its connection.

What you get answered

  • Will our truck finish the buyer's hardest winter route?
  • Does our battery still meet the tender at year 8?
  • How much power does the depot need, and at what hours?

Documents you can take away

A tender asks for the hardest winter route at year 8. You run your truck on that route and hand over the result with every input shown.

How it works

It starts with your routes, not a brochure range

Enter the routes, stops, loads and shift times your vehicles really drive. Everything else is worked out from them.

A truck that is not full by morning stays in the depot

EV Scope checks that every vehicle is full before its shift, with the depot kept under its grid limit.

Too small and the route fails. Too big and you pay for weight

EV Scope sizes the battery to your hardest route, so you compare offers on what you need.

Sized to your hardest route, with margin left at year 8.

The coldest day at year 8 is the one that strands a truck

Cold air, cabin heating and an aged battery are tested together, so you see the worst day before you buy.

Still enough charge on the coldest morning of the year.

Bigger chargers cost more and can force a grid upgrade

EV Scope finds the smallest charger that still has every truck full before its shift. Parked overnight, a small one is often enough.

A heavier battery can leave less room for cargo

Try light, full and changing loads on each route and see the payload left, before you order.

A grid connection can take months or years

EV Scope gives you the power to apply for and the load hour by hour, so you can apply early with the numbers done.

Advice before the money is spent

EV Scope sizes vehicle electrification before anyone signs: the vehicles, the chargers and the grid connection a depot really needs, and what it costs against diesel.

Built on EU methods

Vehicle energy follows the methods of EU Regulation 2017/2400, the standard used to certify the energy use of heavy-duty vehicles.

Conservative by design

Where the data is uncertain, we choose the option that does not underestimate energy use.

Brand-neutral

We don't sell vehicles or chargers. The same numbers work for every supplier.

Every source shown

Each input says where it came from, so a board, a bank or a grid company can check it.

Founded in Copenhagen by an energy engineer from DTU, the Technical University of Denmark.

Privacy

What happens to your data when you use this website and the demo.

Who is responsible

What this website collects

Nothing on its own. The site sets no cookies, has no analytics and loads nothing from other companies. Fonts and images are part of the page.

The company that hosts the site keeps ordinary server logs, such as your IP address and the time of your visit, to run it securely.

What stays in your browser

If you choose a language or switch between day and night, that choice is saved in your browser so the site remembers it. It is not sent to us. Clearing your browser data removes it.

The demo

The demo runs entirely in your browser. What you type into it is not sent anywhere and is gone when you close the page.

When you contact us

The contact form opens your own email app. Nothing reaches us until you send that email. We use what you write to answer you and to follow up, and we keep it only as long as that takes.

Your rights

You can ask to see, correct or delete what we hold about you, or object to how we use it. Write to the email address above.

You can also complain to the Danish Data Protection Agency, Datatilsynet, at datatilsynet.dk.

Last updated 13 November 2026.

Terms of use

These terms cover this website and the demo.

The demo is an illustration

The demo uses a sample fleet and a simplified engine. Its figures show how EV Scope works. They are not advice, and they must not be used to buy vehicles, write a tender or apply for a grid connection.

The website

We keep the content correct as far as we can, but we do not guarantee that it is complete or up to date. Sample figures are marked as illustrative.

Work for customers

Studies and access to the full tool are covered by a separate written agreement.
